correctness.rationale: In the unnormalized L² convention, decomposing m=qℓ+j and applying Parseval over ℓ and the integer translations gives F=Σ_j |Zg(x,ω+j/q)|², a sum rather than its density-normalized average. Zak unitarity makes the optimal constants the essential extrema; continuity makes those the ordinary extrema. Put r=e^(−2πw). Poisson summation of the Fourier exponential gives the two geometric tails with common denominator 1+r²−2r cos(2πx) and nonnegative real coefficients a_s,b_s. With C=Σ(a_s²+b_s²)>0 and E=2Σa_sb_s>=0 the derivative of (C+Eu)/(1+r²−2ru)² in u=cos(2πx) has positive numerator E(1+r²+2ru)+4rC. This forces x=1/2 for the minimum and x=0 for the maximum. On these fibers the ω-dependent part is proportional to r^(2ω)+r^(2/q−2ω), strictly convex and symmetric, giving the unique minimum at 1/(2q) and maximum at the identified endpoints modulo 1/q. At the minimum the sum of q squares cannot vanish because the q frequency translates are distinct and an individual square vanishes only at s=1/2. With c=2πw and R=sinh(c)/sinh(c/q), the extrema simplify to (π/w)²(R−q)/(2 cosh²(c/2)) and (π/w)²(R cosh(c/q)+q)/(2 sinh²(c/2)). Expanding R=q+(q−1/q)c²/6+O_q(c⁴) at zero and using R~exp(c(1−1/q)) at infinity gives all stated leading coefficients and ratios, for fixed q. Replay is analytic in RESULT.md:31–84; VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected, not rerun. Their finite numerical checks cannot establish these global extrema.
